roots.note: 一 = one. It appears in dates, floors, route numbers, and portions that use Sino-Korean numbers.

members.breakdown: 一 one + 人 person + 分 portion

roots.note: 二 = two. Look for 이 in months, floors, subway lines, and measured portions.

members.breakdown: 二 two + 人 person + 分 portion
二 two + 號 line number + 線 line

roots.note: 三 = three. It is the Sino-Korean three used for dates, floors, lines, and portions.

members.breakdown: 三 three + 人 person + 分 portion
三 three + 號 line number + 線 line

roots.note: 四 = four. This 사 is a number, not the 사 in 회사 or 의사.

members.breakdown: 四 four + 人 person + 分 portion

roots.note: 五 = five. It helps decode months, floors, subway lines, and quantities.

members.breakdown: 五 five + 人 person + 分 portion
五 five + 號 line number + 線 line

roots.note: 六 = six. Its regular reading is 육, but 六月 is the fixed exception 유월 (June).

members.breakdown: 六 six + 人 person + 分 portion
六 six + 月 month; special reading 유월

roots.note: 七 = seven. It appears in July, floor numbers, route numbers, and larger counts.

members.breakdown: 七 seven + 號 line number + 線 line

roots.note: 八 = eight. It is common in dates, floors, transit lines, and prices.

members.breakdown: 八 eight + 號 line number + 線 line

roots.note: 九 = nine. This 구 is the number used in September, ninth-floor signs, and Line 9.

members.breakdown: 九 nine + 號 line number + 線 line

roots.note: 十 = ten. Its regular reading is 십, but 十月 is the fixed exception 시월 (October).

members.breakdown: 十 ten + 人 person + 分 portion
十 ten + 月 month; special reading 시월

roots.note: 分 = divide or part. It appears in clock minutes, portions, categories, and separated items.
半 = half. It marks halves of time, events, quantities, and prices.
前 = before or front. Use it to recognize earlier times, front gates, and the first half of something.
後 = after or back. It is common in time labels, medicine directions, rear gates, and later stages.
左 = left. It is the formal direction word used on road signs, maps, and public instructions.

members.breakdown: 左 left + 回 turn + 轉 rotate
左 left + 側 side + 通行 passage

roots.note: 右 = right. It appears in formal directions on roads, station signs, and walking lanes.

members.breakdown: 右 right + 回 turn + 轉 rotate
右 right + 側 side + 通行 passage

roots.note: 東 = east. It helps decode districts, coasts, station exits, and gate names.

members.breakdown: 東 east + 大 great + 門 gate

roots.note: 西 = west. It appears in regional names, coasts, districts, and historic gates.

members.breakdown: 西 west + 大 great + 門 gate

roots.note: 南 = south. It is common in place names, regional notices, and directions.

members.breakdown: 南 south + 大 great + 門 gate

roots.note: 北 = north. It appears in place names, regional weather, and directions.

members.english: north of the Han River; Gangbuk

roots.note: 入 = enter. It is one of the most useful sign roots: entrances, admission, hospitalization, immigration, and input.

members.breakdown: 入 put in + 力 power

roots.note: 出 = go out. It unlocks exit signs, departures, access, commuting, and output.

members.breakdown: 出 go out + 發 start
出 go out + 勤 work
出 put out + 力 power

roots.note: 口 = mouth or opening. In daily signs it often means an entrance, exit, counter, or population count.
路 = route or path. Inside words it is usually 로; at the start of a word it can become 노, as in 노선.

members.breakdown: 經 pass through + 路 route

roots.note: 道 = way or road. It appears in road types and transport routes rather than naming one specific street.

members.breakdown: 高速 high speed + 道路 road

roots.note: 驛 = train or subway station. It is different from 정류장, which is a bus stop.

members.breakdown: 地下鐵 subway + 驛 station
驛 station + 勢 influence + 圈 area

roots.note: 線 = line. It connects subway routes, transit routes, tracks, wires, and drawn lines.
交 = cross or exchange. It is common in transportation, intersections, exchanges, and changing shifts.

members.breakdown: 交 cross + 叉 fork + 路 road

roots.note: 通 = pass through or connect. It appears in traffic, phone calls, passage, ordinary status, and bankbooks.
運 = move or carry. It is central to driving, transit operation, shipping, exercise, and luck.
行 = go or carry out. This 행 appears in banks, travel, transit operation, passage, and walking.
號 = assigned number or signal. It is used for rooms, phone numbers, signals, and numbered subway lines.

members.breakdown: 電話 telephone + 番號 number
病室 hospital room + 番號 number

roots.note: 層 = floor or layer. It is essential for elevators, apartment notices, and building descriptions.

members.breakdown: 層 floor + 間 between + 騷音 noise

roots.note: 家 = household, home, or a person skilled in a field. Context tells which meaning is active.
住 = reside. It appears throughout addresses, resident services, housing, and registration forms.
居 = dwell. It helps decode residence, living space, cohabitation, and address-related terms.
所 = place or office. It appears in addresses, service offices, research centers, and police boxes.
管 = manage or tube. It connects building management, storage, jurisdiction, and water pipes.

members.breakdown: 水道 water supply + 管 pipe

roots.note: 理 = put in order or make sense of something. It appears in management, cooking, organizing, repair, and processing.

members.breakdown: 修 fix + 理 put right

roots.note: 公 = public or official. It is common in parks, public services, official forms, and public holidays.

members.breakdown: 公 public + 務 work + 員 member

roots.note: 共 = together or shared. It appears in shared spaces, common features, and public-use facilities.
安 = safe or calm. It connects safety notices with relief, security, anxiety, and stability.
全 = whole or complete. It appears in safety, totals, nationwide notices, and complete states.
危 = danger. It marks hazards, crises, urgent conditions, and dangerous materials.
險 = danger or risk. It appears in warnings, insurance, adventures, and descriptions of rough conditions.
禁 = forbid. It is one of the clearest roots on public signs: no entry, no smoking, and prohibited areas.

members.breakdown: 出入 access + 禁止 prohibited
禁止 prohibited + 區域 zone

roots.note: 止 = stop. It appears on prohibition, stop, suspension, and prevention notices.

members.breakdown: 一時 temporary + 停止 stop

roots.note: 注 = pour in or focus on. It links warnings, injections, orders, and input into a container or system.

members.breakdown: 注意 caution + 事項 items

roots.note: 意 = thought or intention. It helps separate attention, meaning, opinions, intentions, and agreement.
開 = open. It appears in opening hours, new service, unsealing packages, and public release.

members.english: opening of a route or service

roots.note: 閉 = close. It appears in closures, businesses shutting down, and sealed spaces.
休 = rest. It is common on holiday notices, closed-day signs, rest areas, and business breaks.

members.english: closed for the day; off duty

roots.note: 定 = set or decide. It appears in schedules, decisions, regular service, designated places, and confirmations.
店 = shop or branch. It helps with store signs, staff labels, opening, closing, and branch names.
市 = city or market. It appears in city centers, local government, residents, and traditional markets.
費 = expense. It appears in bills for transport, food, housing management, and memberships.
價 = price or value. It connects prices with fixed, low, and high price labels.
品 = goods or product. It is useful on shopping, food, parcel, and sold-out notices.

members.breakdown: 品 product + 切 cut off

roots.note: 買 = buy. It appears in purchase buttons, buyer labels, stock intake, and buying-and-selling terms.

members.breakdown: 買 buy + 入 bring in

roots.note: 賣 = sell. It appears in listings, stores, sales figures, and transaction language.
用 = use or purpose. It appears in using services, practical use, costs, and shared facilities.

members.english: use of a service or facility

roots.note: 無 = none or without. It appears in free services, unmanned facilities, wireless access, and no-condition labels.
有 = have or exist. It appears in paid services, validity, ownership, holdings, and being well-known.

members.breakdown: 所 that which + 有 have

roots.note: 可 = possible or permitted. It is extremely useful on reservation, parking, entry, and service-availability notices.

members.breakdown: 駐車 parking + 可能 available

roots.note: 能 = ability. It appears in possibility, skills, device functions, performance, and competence.
醫 = medicine or doctor. This 의 is the medical root in doctors, clinics, treatment, and pharmaceuticals.

members.breakdown: 醫 medicine + 藥 drug + 品 product

roots.note: 院 = institution or enclosed facility. It appears in hospitals, clinics, admission, discharge, and academies.
症 = symptom or medical condition. It appears in intake questions, pain descriptions, and aftereffects.

members.breakdown: 後 after + 遺 remain + 症 condition

roots.note: 熱 = heat or fever. It helps with symptom questions, temperature warnings, and fever medicine.

members.breakdown: 解 remove + 熱 fever + 劑 medicine

roots.note: 血 = blood. It is common in health checks, test results, bleeding, blood sugar, and anemia.
氣 = air, energy, or condition. It connects mood, air, electricity, outdoor temperature, and colds.
健 = healthy or strong. It appears in health, public health, checkups, and sound or wholesome conditions.

members.breakdown: 健康 health + 檢診 examination

roots.note: 診 = medically examine. It unlocks treatment, diagnosis, checkups, intake questions, and examinations.
雨 = rain. It appears in umbrellas, rain notices, rainfall totals, heavy rain, and weather alerts.
雪 = snow. It is used in heavy-snow alerts, accumulation reports, and snow-removal notices.
風 = wind. It appears in typhoons, strong-wind alerts, wind speed, ventilation, and scenery.

members.breakdown: 颱 great storm + 風 wind

roots.note: 溫 = warm or temperature. It appears on weather reports, thermostats, medical checks, and hot-water controls.
配 = distribute or assign. It appears in deliveries, shipping, placement, handouts, and assigned times or rooms.

members.breakdown: 配 distribute + 付 hand over

roots.note: 送 = send. It connects parcel delivery, transportation, money transfers, data transfer, and broadcasting.
親 = close or related. It appears in friends, kindness, relatives, familiarity, and being close to someone.
